method: For gamma-encoded 8-bit R′G′B′, luma is Y′ = Kr R′ + (1 − Kr − Kb) G′ + Kb B′ on channels normalized to 0–1. Cb = (B′ − Y′) / (2(1 − Kb)) and Cr = (R′ − Y′) / (2(1 − Kr)). BT.601 uses Kr 0.299 and Kb 0.114, BT.709 uses 0.2126 and 0.0722, and BT.2020 non-constant-luminance conversion uses 0.2627 and 0.058. Limited range emits 16 + 219Y′ and 128 + 224Cb/Cr; full range emits 255Y′ and 127.5 + 255Cb/Cr. Codes are rounded to the nearest integer and clipped to their selected 8-bit ranges. Inverse conversion algebraically reconstructs R′ and B′ from Cr and Cb, then G′ from luma, and flags any unrounded RGB channel outside 0–255 before clipping. The round trip uses the quantized output codes. This tool does not linearize RGB, change transfer characteristics or primaries, process constant-luminance Y′CbcCrc, interpret HDR metadata, or decode media.
